sources: Grid CO2: 478 gCO2eq/kWh (lowcarbonpower.org 2025); thermal energy from 60% coal boilers. Water: moderate cotton/synthetic mix (ICAC, Water Footprint Network). Labor: ITUC GRI 2024 rating 5, but min wage ~$370/mo offset by enforcement gaps. Transparency: limited supply chain disclosure (Fashion Revolution 2024).

Grid CO2: 595 gCO2eq/kWh (lowcarbonpower.org 2025, coal-dominant 75%). Water: cotton-intensive production, high blue water footprint (Chapagain et al., Water Footprint Network). Labor: ITUC GRI 2024 rating 5, garment min wage ~$110-175/mo varies by state. Transparency: some large exporters disclose but informal sector dominant.

Grid CO2: 584 gCO2eq/kWh (lowcarbonpower.org 2024, gas+coal 86%). Water: cotton processing intensive (PLOS Sustainability 2023). Labor: ITUC 2024 worst-10 country, min wage BDT 12,500/mo (~$113) raised 2023 from $95 (Cornell GLI 2024). Transparency: post-Rana Plaza improvements but still low systemic disclosure.

Grid CO2: 447 gCO2eq/kWh (lowcarbonpower.org 2024). Water: synthetic-heavy production mix, lower than cotton countries. Labor: min wage $141-204/mo by region (Sourcingjournal 2024), moderate enforcement. Transparency: growing FDI-driven disclosure requirements.

Grid CO2: 392 gCO2eq/kWh (lowcarbonpower.org 2024). Water: cotton+synthetic mix, irrigation-dependent cotton in SE Anatolia. Labor: ITUC 2024 worst-10 country, but min wage ~$450/mo; severe union suppression. Transparency: EU-adjacent disclosure norms, some supply chain mapping.

Grid CO2: 346 gCO2eq/kWh (lowcarbonpower.org 2024) but heavy thermal/gas for textile steam. Water: Indus basin cotton extremely water-intensive (Water Footprint Network: 97% of basin water to cotton). Labor: ITUC GRI 2024 rating 4, garment min wage ~$100/mo. Transparency: informal sector dominant, minimal disclosure.

Grid CO2: 625 gCO2eq/kWh (lowcarbonpower.org 2023, coal-heavy). Water: synthetic-focused production. Labor: ITUC notes Omnibus Law removed min wage protections (2024), ~$150-250/mo varies. Transparency: limited systemic disclosure despite large export sector.

Grid CO2: 109 gCO2eq/kWh (lowcarbonpower.org 2024, hydro-dominant). Water: cotton water footprint 3,436 L/kg lint, lowest globally due to rain-fed (Cotton Brazil/ICAC). Labor: ITUC 2024 rating improved to 4, min wage ~$260/mo, better enforcement than Asian peers. Transparency: moderate, some brands in FTI.

Grid CO2: 479 gCO2eq/kWh (lowcarbonpower.org 2024, gas 50%+). Water: synthetic/polyester-heavy mix. Labor: min wage ~$300/mo (2024), moderate protections but migrant worker exploitation documented. Transparency: some FDI-driven reporting.

Grid CO2: 472 gCO2eq/kWh (lowcarbonpower.org 2024, coal 40%+). Water: garment assembly focus, moderate water use. Labor: min wage $204/mo (2024), union leaders arrested (ITUC 2024). Transparency: Better Factories Cambodia (ILO) provides some monitoring but limited brand-level disclosure.

Grid CO2: 396 gCO2eq/kWh (lowcarbonpower.org 2025). Water: high-tech synthetic production, efficient water use. Labor: min wage ~$1,600/mo (2024), ITUC noted trade unionist killed. Transparency: K-fashion brands improving ESG disclosure, Samsung/LG supply chain standards.

Grid CO2: 324 gCO2eq/kWh (lowcarbonpower.org 2025). Water: luxury/high-value textile focus, advanced water treatment (Fulgar 2024). Labor: strong EU labor protections, min ~$1,800/mo equivalent. Transparency: Gucci 74%, OVS top scorers in FTI 2024 (Fashion Revolution).

Grid CO2: 298 gCO2eq/kWh (lowcarbonpower.org 2025, renewables 55%+). Water: technical textiles, advanced closed-loop systems. Labor: strong labor laws, works councils, min wage EUR 12.41/hr. Transparency: Puma 75% top FTI scorer, Adidas 55%, German Supply Chain Act (LkSG) 2023.

Grid CO2: 348 gCO2eq/kWh (lowcarbonpower.org 2025). Water: SE cotton 234 L/kg irrigated vs West 3,272 L/kg (EIA). Labor: federal min wage $7.25/hr but most states higher, OSHA enforcement. Transparency: major brands HQ (Nike, Gap, PVH) score 40-60% in FTI 2024.

Grid CO2: 412 gCO2eq/kWh (lowcarbonpower.org 2025). Water: cotton/synthetic mix, drought stress. Labor: ITUC 2024 noted deterioration, min wage ~$375/mo (2024), USMCA labor reforms ongoing. Transparency: maquiladora sector has limited disclosure.

Grid CO2: 310 gCO2eq/kWh (lowcarbonpower.org 2024). Water: garment-focused (less spinning), moderate. Labor: ITUC 2024 noted union removal from advisory council, min wage ~$75/mo but higher in FTZ. Transparency: ethical sourcing positioning, some MAS Holdings-type disclosure.

Grid CO2: 342 gCO2eq/kWh (lowcarbonpower.org 2024, gas 51%). Water: garment assembly focus. Labor: ITUC 2024 rating 5+ (no guarantee of rights), military coup decimated protections, min wage ~$60/mo. Transparency: near-zero due to political crisis, brands exiting.

Grid CO2: 24 gCO2eq/kWh (lowcarbonpower.org 2023, 96% hydro). Water: cotton cultivation in Awash basin, water-intensive. Labor: garment min wage ~$26-60/mo (ILO), no statutory minimum, Hawassa industrial park documented issues. Transparency: nascent export sector, minimal disclosure frameworks.

Grid CO2: 446 gCO2eq/kWh (lowcarbonpower.org 2024). Water: Nile delta cotton among highest blue water footprint globally (Water Footprint Network). Labor: ITUC 2024 worst-10 country, union suppression, min wage ~$130/mo. Transparency: limited, state-influenced textile sector.

Grid CO2: 551 gCO2eq/kWh (lowcarbonpower.org 2024, coal 50%+). Water: garment/cut-and-sew focus, moderate. Labor: min wage ~$280/mo, ITUC GRI rating 4, some protections but enforcement gaps. Transparency: EU proximity drives some compliance but limited systemic disclosure.
